themes.theme: Setting up a timer that cues you every 30 seconds for a whole session, hands-free
themes.hook: You want a buzz every 30 seconds for the next half hour without touching your watch once — here is how to build that instead of restarting a stopwatch 60 times.
themes.evidence: r/AppleWatch thread asking for an app that notifies every 30 seconds for a set duration with no interaction drew 26 replies and ended with the poster marking it SOLVED only after app suggestions.
pain_quotes: Wants to start a session and then never touch the watch again until it is over.
The stock timer has to be dismissed each time it fires, which breaks the interval.
Would pay for an app but cannot find one that repeats a short interval automatically.
themes.distinctFrom: best-tabata-timer (0.26) is a buying guide asking which 20/10 app to install; this post answers the setup question of how to make any fixed 30-second cadence repeat unattended for a whole session, including odd totals that are not eight rounds.
themes.searchEvidence: Keyword research: '30 second interval timer' 5400/mo, LOW competition; supporting '1 minute interval timer' 1900/mo and 'repeat timer' 1600/mo.
themes.imagePrompt: A person mid-burpee on a rubber gym floor in a bright home garage gym, wrist raised slightly, motion blur on the arms, morning light through an open roller door

themes.theme: Running intervals on vibration cues alone when beeps are not an option
themes.hook: Shared gyms, early mornings and quiet offices all rule out beeping — here is how to run a full interval session on haptics you can feel but nobody else can hear.
themes.evidence: An r/AppleWatch post asking for a timer that vibrates once and stops on its own hit 40 upvotes and 28 comments; a second thread specifically wanted a custom interval that only buzzes the watch and never sounds.
pain_quotes: The native timer keeps buzzing until it is dismissed, which forces you to look at the wrist.
Needs a discreet cue that fires once and clears itself in a room where sound would be rude.
Wants haptics on the watch only, with the phone staying silent in a pocket.
themes.distinctFrom: interval-timer-with-music (0.19) answers how to hear cues over a playlist; this post answers the opposite question of how to run the same session with no audio at all, and what a haptic pattern has to do to replace a countdown beep.
themes.searchEvidence: Pain-signal led. Supporting striking distance: 'interval timer apple watch' 3 impressions at position 27.3 over 90 days, the cluster this phrasing sits inside.
themes.imagePrompt: Close-up of a person's forearm and hand gripping a kettlebell handle at the bottom of a swing, dim early-morning apartment living room, soft window light, no devices visible

themes.theme: When the Apple Watch Workout app's built-in intervals are enough and when they are not
themes.hook: watchOS has interval support built in, so the honest question is where it stops being enough — and the answer is more specific than 'get an app'.
themes.evidence: An r/AppleWatch user timing yoga holds and lifting rest with the Workout app's interval feature reported the haptic feedback silently dying mid-session a couple of times a month; another could not start a custom Workout-app interval from a Shortcut at all.
pain_quotes: The built-in interval haptics stop firing partway through a session with no warning.
Custom workouts built in the Workout app cannot be launched from an automation.
Ends up counting in their head or staring at the wrist mid-pose when the cue fails.
themes.distinctFrom: best-apple-watch-interval-timer (0.25) is a buying guide ranking third-party apps against each other; this post compares Apple's own built-in Workout-app intervals against the third-party category as a whole, and names the specific limits — nested blocks, per-phase cues, reuse — where the stock feature runs out.
themes.searchEvidence: Striking distance: 'interval timer apple watch' 3 impressions at position 27.3, 'interval timer on apple watch' 2 impressions at position 38.5, 'workout timer apple watch' position 33 (90 days).
themes.imagePrompt: A person holding a low lunge stretch on a yoga mat in a sunlit spare room, wrist resting on the front knee, plants and a water bottle in the background

themes.theme: Making the timer screen tell you what you are doing now and what is next
themes.hook: A number counting down tells you nothing if you cannot remember which move it belongs to — here is how to build intervals that name the current exercise and the one coming up.
themes.evidence: A coach on r/crossfit described hunting for an iPad interval timer that shows the current move plus the next one with full setup cues, because Seconds Pro truncates the label text they need.
pain_quotes: Wants the current movement and the upcoming movement both visible, not just a countdown.
Needs room for a full coaching cue like foot position and bracing, not a two-word label.
The app they use now cuts the script off halfway through.
themes.distinctFrom: creating-saving-custom-hiit-workouts (0.13) covers building and saving a session at all; this post is specifically about the labelling layer — naming each phase, previewing the next one, and how much text actually survives on a watch face versus a phone.
themes.searchEvidence: Pain-signal led. Supporting striking distance: 'tabata timer exercises' at position 41 and 'personalized hiit workout' at position 21 over 90 days.
themes.imagePrompt: An iPad propped on a weight bench facing a small group gym floor, two people mid-squat in the background out of focus, industrial windows, screen angled away from the camera

themes.theme: Timing rest between strength sets so it stops drifting from 90 seconds to four minutes
themes.hook: Rest is the part of a lifting session nobody times honestly, and the gap between what you think you took and what you actually took is usually enormous.
themes.evidence: An r/AppleWatch thread asked for an app that times a work period and a rest period together and could not find one that also survived being started by automation; another wanted a 25-on/5-off block repeated sixteen times with wrist-only alerts.
pain_quotes: Wants one app that handles the working set and the rest, not two separate stopwatches.
Rest between sets stretches out whenever they look at their phone.
Needs a long repeating work-and-rest block that runs for an hour without resetting.
themes.distinctFrom: interval-timer-repeating-sets (0.19) is about building multi-block interval sessions where work is the point; this post is about strength training, where the work is rep-based and the only thing being timed is the recovery between sets.
themes.searchEvidence: Keyword research: 'workout timer' 2900/mo MEDIUM, 'exercise timer' 1300/mo LOW, 'repeat timer' 1600/mo LOW.
themes.imagePrompt: A lifter sitting on a bench beside a loaded barbell in a chalky commercial gym, forearms on knees, catching their breath between sets, warm overhead lighting

themes.theme: Actually running a Tabata timer: prep phase, round counting and what each cue means
themes.hook: Twenty on, ten off, eight rounds is easy to say and surprisingly easy to run wrong — most people lose the count somewhere around round five.
themes.query: what is a tabata timer and how do you use it
themes.evidence: Search Console shows people reaching the site on 'what is tabata timer' and 'how to use tabata timer', and r/AppleWatch has a long-running complaint about not finding a simple Tabata app without a subscription.
pain_quotes: Knows the 20/10 numbers but not where the prep countdown or the round counter fit.
Loses track of which round they are on once the effort gets high.
Cannot tell from the beeps alone whether a phase is work or rest.
themes.distinctFrom: best-tabata-timer (0.25) answers which Tabata app to pick; this post assumes you already have one open and answers how to drive it — prep length, round indexing, what to do when a session is not eight rounds, and which cue means what.
themes.searchEvidence: Striking distance: 'what is tabata timer' 3 impressions at position 36.3, 'tabata timing' at position 32, 'how to use tabata timer' at position 37 (90 days).
themes.imagePrompt: Overhead view of a person mid mountain-climber on a mat in a garage gym, one dumbbell and a towel just outside the mat, concrete floor, hard side lighting

themes.theme: Building treadmill speed and incline intervals when the console will not do what you want
themes.hook: Gym treadmill programs give you someone else's intervals; here is how to run your own blocks off a timer and just change the belt when it tells you to.
themes.evidence: Running-interval demand is the largest keyword cluster feeding our strongest app-lane post, and gym-floor threads repeatedly describe fighting a treadmill console instead of following a plan.
pain_quotes: The built-in treadmill programs never match the work-to-rest ratio they actually want.
Loses the plan halfway through because they are doing mental maths at 12 kph.
Wants a cue that says change now rather than watching the console clock.
themes.distinctFrom: how-to-build-a-running-interval-workout-on-apple-watch (0.13) covers outdoor running where pace and distance come from GPS; this post is about the treadmill, where the belt controls speed and the only thing your timer can do is tell you when to change it.
themes.searchEvidence: Keyword research seeded from our best-performing app-lane post: 'interval running workouts' 14800/mo LOW, 'interval running training' 14800/mo LOW.
themes.imagePrompt: A runner at a hard effort on a gym treadmill seen from the side at hip height, shoes and belt in motion blur, row of empty machines receding behind, cool gym lighting
